_meta: Machinevertaling (nl naar en) van de eigen factcheck von-der-leyen-epstein van Factiz, eigen werk van de redactie (B82, B84), door claude-sonnet-5-5, eigenvertaling-v1; doublecheck/eigenvertaling.py, PLAN #37.8.

velden.kop: Image of Ursula von der Leyen with Jeffrey Epstein was made with AI
velden.oordeel_zin: The image carries an AI watermark, was already on Facebook in July with an AI label, and the numbers on it do not appear in the Epstein files [1] [2] [11].
velden.bewering: This photo from the Epstein files shows Ursula von der Leyen with Jeffrey Epstein.
velden.kort: Since 7 October, an image of Ursula von der Leyen with Jeffrey Epstein has been circulating in Dutch on X, with a file number and a document number on it [10]. The image was made with AI: it has been on Facebook since 12 July with a label for AI content, and newsrooms found an invisible AI watermark in it [11] [1] [2]. The numbers on the image do not appear in the Epstein files released by the US Department of Justice [1] [3] [6].
velden.tekst:
On Wednesday 7 October 2026 at 23:21, a Dutch-language post appeared on X with an image of Ursula von der Leyen, the President of the European Commission, next to Jeffrey Epstein [10]. The image shows a file number and a document number, which are meant to suggest that it comes from the Epstein files [1] [4].

The image is older than the post. The earliest copy that newsrooms found has been on Facebook since 12 July 2026, posted by a private individual, with the label that Meta places on content made with AI [11] [1]. A day later it was on the French-language site of the Pravda network [1]. That is a network of pro-Russian sites that pose as a news outlet [9]. The image then circulated in Italian, Spanish, German, English, Georgian and Russian, among other languages [1] [2] [4] [5].

The Italian outlet Open and the Spanish outlet Maldita.es found SynthID in the image [1] [2]. That is an invisible watermark that Google adds to images made or edited with its AI [8]. Lead Stories and TheJournal.ie also reported an AI watermark [3] [4]. Open found no real photo of the two together in press archives or in the released documents [1].

Now the numbers. The US Department of Justice puts the documents from the Epstein investigation online in the Epstein Library [6]. In January 2026, about 3 million pages were added there, after earlier releases [7]. According to Open, Lead Stories and Myth Detector, the numbers on the image do not appear in those documents, and the department uses a very different numbering [1] [3] [5].

The Dutch post came almost three months after the first check we found, from Open on 15 July, and five weeks after the one from Lead Stories [1] [3] [10]. We did not find a check in Dutch.
velden.niet_weten: We do not know who made the image. Lead Stories and TheJournal.ie report that a program from OpenAI found the SynthID watermark [3] [4]. SynthID belongs to Google [8]; why a program from OpenAI reports it, we do not know. That does not change the verdict: Open and Maldita.es found the watermark with Google's programs [1] [2].
nog_uitzoeken: Which version of the image the post showed, black-and-white or in color, and what text accompanied it. The post is gone.
tijdlijn: The Department of Justice puts about 3 million pages on Epstein online [7].
The image on Facebook, with Meta's label for AI content [11] [1].
The image on the French-language site of the Pravda network [1].
Open: the image was made with AI [1].
Lead Stories: made with AI, numbers not in the files [3].
TheJournal.ie: made with AI, shared more than a thousand times on Facebook [4].
Myth Detector: the image circulates in Georgian and Russian [5].
